verdict.rationale: Docs show building blocks that support updates — customId dedup/update for documents ('intelligently processes only what's new'), isStatic vs dynamic memory flags, and 'living knowledge graph' / auto-updating user profiles built from ongoing interactions — but there is no explicit documented mechanism for detecting contradictory facts and merging/superseding them. One comparison-page line even lists 'No temporal truth ("loved Adidas" then "switched to Puma", both stay equally relevant)' which is ambiguous as to whether it describes Supermemory itself or a competitor, undermining confidence that contradiction resolution is a confirmed, documented capability. Missing for 10: explicit contradiction-detection/merge algorithm, first-party or independent example of an old fact being superseded, clarification that the 'no temporal truth' limitation doesn't apply to Supermemory itself.
